error: Error: Dynamic server usage: Route couldn't be rendered statically because it used cookies
meaning: During next build, Next.js tried to pre-render a page as static HTML, but the code reads per-request data (cookies(), headers(), searchParams), which only exist at request time.
causes: A Supabase server client reading cookies inside a page or layout that Next.js assumed was static.
export const dynamic = 'error' or generateStaticParams forcing static rendering.
A try/catch around cookies() that swallowed Next's internal bail-out signal.

steps.text: If the page needs the logged-in user, mark it dynamic.
Don't wrap cookies()/headers() in try/catch that hides the error; let Next handle it.
Keep auth-dependent reads out of the root layout if other pages should stay static. Move them into the page or a component under a dynamic route.
For public pages, fetch data without cookies (a plain client using the anon key) so they can stay static.

prompt: next build fails with 'Dynamic server usage: Route <ROUTE> couldn't be rendered statically because it used cookies'. Mark the routes that need the user session with export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic', remove any try/catch around cookies()/headers(), and move session reads out of the root layout so public pages can stay static.

faq.a: The page renders per request instead of once at build, which is normal for logged-in pages.
Often it's logged during build; it fails only when static rendering is enforced or the error is caught incorrectly.
